title.raw: 卷八十四 列傳第七十二: 孝行 Volume 84 Biographies 72: Filial Acts

sentences.zh: 列傳第七十二孝行

translations.literal: Biography 72: Filial Conduct
translations.idiomatic: Biography 72: Acts of Filial Piety

sentences.zh: 長孫慮乞伏保孫益德董洛生楊引閻元明吳悉達王續生李顯達倉跋張升王崇郭文恭荊可秦族皇甫遐張元王頒弟頍楊慶田翼紐因劉仕俊翟普林華秋徐孝肅

translations.literal: Zhangsun Lü, Qifu Bao, Sun Yide, Dong Luosheng, Yang Yin, Yan Yuanming, Wu Xida, Wang Xusheng, Li Xianda, Cang Ba, Zhang Sheng, Wang Chong, Guo Wengong, Jing Ke, Qin Zu, Huangfu Xia, Zhang Yuan, Wang Ban and his younger brother Hui, Yang Qing, Tian Yi, Niu Yin, Liu Shijun, Zhai Pulü, Hua Qiu, and Xu Xiaosu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Lü; Qifu Bao; Sun Yide; Dong Luosheng; Yang Yin; Yan Yuanming; Wu Xida; Wang Xusheng; Li Xianda; Cang Ba; Zhang Sheng; Wang Chong; Guo Wengong; Jing Ke; Qin Zu; Huangfu Xia; Zhang Yuan; Wang Ban and his younger brother Hui; Yang Qing; Tian Yi; Niu Yin; Liu Shijun; Zhai Pulü; Hua Qiu; and Xu Xiaosu.

sentences.zh: 《孝經》云：「夫孝，天之經也，地之義也，人之行也。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "Filial piety is the constant of Heaven, the righteousness of Earth, and the conduct of humanity."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety declares: "Filial piety is Heaven's enduring law, Earth's rightful order, and the proper way of human life."

sentences.zh: 」《論語》云：「君子務本，本立而道生，孝悌也者，其為仁之本歟！

translations.literal: The Analects says: "The gentleman devotes himself to the root; when the root is established, the Way arises. Are not filial piety and brotherly respect the root of humaneness!"
translations.idiomatic: The Analects teaches: "The gentleman attends to the foundation; once it stands firm, the Way comes to life. Are not filial devotion and respect among siblings the very root of humaneness?"

sentences.zh: 」《呂覽》云：「夫孝，三皇五帝之本務，萬事之納紀也。

translations.literal: The Lüshi Chunqiu says: "Filial piety is the fundamental task of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, the guiding principle of all affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The Lüshi Chunqiu states: "Filial piety was the essential duty of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, the thread that binds every undertaking."

sentences.zh: 執一術而百善至，百邪去，天下順者，其唯孝乎！

translations.literal: Hold to this one practice and a hundred virtues arrive, a hundred evils depart, and the realm is brought into accord—can this be anything but filial piety!
translations.idiomatic: Uphold this single practice and every virtue follows, every vice falls away, and the world falls into harmony—what else could accomplish that but filial piety!

sentences.zh: 」然則孝之為德至矣，其為道遠矣，其化人深矣。

translations.literal: Thus filial piety as a virtue is utmost; as a Way it is far-reaching; in transforming people it is profound.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety, then, is the highest of virtues, the farthest-reaching of ways, and the deepest force in shaping human hearts.

sentences.zh: 故聖帝明王行之于四海，則與天地合其德，與日月齊其明；

translations.literal: Therefore when sage emperors and enlightened kings practice it throughout the four seas, their virtue joins with Heaven and Earth and their brilliance equals sun and moon;
translations.idiomatic: When sage emperors and enlightened kings practice it across the realm, their virtue merges with Heaven and Earth and their radiance rivals the sun and moon;

sentences.zh: 諸侯卿大夫行之于國家，則永保其宗社，長守其祿位；

translations.literal: when feudal lords, ministers, and grand masters practice it within their states, they forever preserve their ancestral altars and long hold their stipends and offices;
translations.idiomatic: when feudal lords, ministers, and grand masters practice it within their domains, they secure their ancestral altars in perpetuity and keep their ranks and emoluments for generations;

sentences.zh: 匹夫匹婦行之于閭閻，則播徽烈于當年，揚休名於千載。

translations.literal: when common men and women practice it in their lanes and wards, they spread fine renown in their own age and raise their excellent names for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: when ordinary men and women practice it in village and lane, they win shining repute in their own day and leave honored names for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 是以堯、舜、湯、武居帝王之位，垂至德以敦其風；

translations.literal: Thus Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu, occupying the throne of emperors and kings, extended utmost virtue to thicken their customs;
translations.idiomatic: Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu sat upon the imperial throne and spread supreme virtue to deepen the moral climate of their age;

sentences.zh: 孔、墨、荀、孟稟聖賢之資，弘正道以勵其俗。

translations.literal: Confucius, Mozi, Xunzi, and Mencius received the endowment of sages and worthies and enlarged the correct Way to encourage their peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius, Mozi, Xunzi, and Mencius were endowed with the gifts of sages and worthies and championed the true Way to stir their contemporaries toward better conduct.

sentences.zh: 觀其所由，在此而已矣。

translations.literal: Observe whence they acted—it is in this alone.
translations.idiomatic: Look to the source of their achievement, and you will find it here and nowhere else.

sentences.zh: 然而淳源既往，澆風愈扇，禮義不樹，廉讓莫修。

translations.literal: Yet the pure source has long since passed away, the corrupting wind blows ever stronger, ritual and righteousness are not planted, and modest yielding is not cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the age of pristine virtue is gone, decadent fashions spread ever wider, ritual and righteousness go unplanted, and humility and forbearance find no cultivation.

sentences.zh: 若乃綰銀黃，列鐘鼎，立於朝廷之間，非一族也；

translations.literal: As for those who fasten silver seals and yellow cords, array bronze bells and tripods, and stand in the court—there is more than one such clan;
translations.idiomatic: Those who wear official seals, display bronze bells and tripods, and stand in the imperial court are hardly few;

sentences.zh: 積龜貝，實倉廩，居於閭巷之內，非一家也。

translations.literal: those who heap tortoise shells and cowries and fill their granaries, dwelling within lanes and alleys—there is more than one such household.
translations.idiomatic: those who stockpile tortoise shells and cowries and fill their granaries, living in village lanes, are hardly rare either.

sentences.zh: 其於愛敬之道，則有未能備焉。

translations.literal: In the way of love and reverence, there are those who have not yet attained completeness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the practice of loving and revering their parents, many still fall short.

sentences.zh: 哀思之節，罕有得其中焉。

translations.literal: In the observance of grief and remembrance, few attain the mean.
translations.idiomatic: In the proper measure of mourning and remembrance, few truly hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 斯乃詩人所以思素冠，孔門有以責衣錦也。

translations.literal: This is why the poets yearn for the plain cap, and why Confucius's school had reason to reproach those who wore brocade.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the poets mourned the man in plain hemp, and why Confucius's disciples had cause to rebuke those who paraded in brocade while their parents still lived.

sentences.zh: 且生盡色養之方，終極哀思之地，厥跡多緒，其心一焉。

translations.literal: Moreover, in life one exhausts the methods of cheerful nurture; in death one reaches the utmost of grief and remembrance—their traces are many-threaded, but their heart is one.
translations.idiomatic: In life they give their utmost to honoring parents with joy; in death they carry mourning to its fullest limit—the outward forms vary, but the inward purpose is one.

sentences.zh: 若乃誠達泉魚，感通鳥獸，事匪常倫，斯蓋希矣。

translations.literal: As for sincerity reaching fish in the springs and moving birds and beasts—affairs outside ordinary norms—such cases are surely rare.
translations.idiomatic: When sincerity moves fish in hidden springs or stirs birds and beasts—deeds beyond ordinary human measure—such cases are exceedingly rare.

sentences.zh: 至如溫床、扇席，灌樹、負土，苟或加人，咸疾俗。

translations.literal: As for warming the bed, fanning the mat, watering the tree, and carrying earth on one's back—if anyone adds to these, all alike despise such show.
translations.idiomatic: Acts such as warming the parental bed, fanning the sleeping mat, watering a parent's tree, or carrying earth for a grave—whenever someone goes further still, the world brands it vulgar ostentation.

sentences.zh: 斯固仁人君子所以興歎，哲後賢宰所宜屬心。

translations.literal: This is indeed what benevolent gentlemen sigh over and what wise rulers and worthy ministers ought to set their hearts upon.
translations.idiomatic: This is precisely what humane gentlemen lament and what wise sovereigns and worthy ministers ought to take to heart.

sentences.zh: 如令明教化以救其弊，優爵賞以勸其心，存懇誠以誘其進，積歲月以求其終，則今之所謂少者，可以為多矣；

translations.literal: If one were to clarify teaching and transformation to remedy these ills, confer preferential ranks and rewards to encourage their hearts, preserve earnest sincerity to lure them forward, and accumulate years to seek the final result, then what is now called few could become many;
translations.idiomatic: Were rulers to clarify moral instruction to cure these ills, grant preferential honors to stir people's hearts, cherish sincere devotion to draw them onward, and allow years to pass until the habit took root, then those now deemed few in number could become many;

sentences.zh: 古之所謂難者，可以為易矣。

translations.literal: what the ancients called difficult could become easy.
translations.idiomatic: and what the ancients called difficult could be made easy.

sentences.zh: 長孫慮等闕稽古之學，無俊偉之才。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Lü and the others lack learning that investigates antiquity and possess no outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Lü and his fellows had no training in classical learning and no towering gifts of intellect.

sentences.zh: 或任其自然，情無矯飾；

translations.literal: Some followed their natural disposition, their feelings free of pretense;
translations.idiomatic: Some simply followed their inborn nature, with no artifice in their feelings;

sentences.zh: 或篤於天性，勤其四體。

translations.literal: some were deeply devoted to their inborn nature and labored with all four limbs.
translations.idiomatic: others were profoundly devoted by nature and toiled with their whole bodies.

sentences.zh: 並竭股肱之力，咸盡愛敬之心，自足膝下之歡，忘懷軒冕之貴。

translations.literal: All alike exhausted the strength of arms and legs and fully discharged hearts of love and reverence, finding sufficiency in the joy beneath their parents' knees and forgetting the honor of cap and carriage.
translations.idiomatic: All alike poured out their bodily strength and gave their full measure of love and reverence, content with the happiness of serving at their parents' feet and heedless of the glory of high office.

sentences.zh: 不言而化，人神通感。

translations.literal: Without words they transformed others; spirits and men were moved in sympathy.
translations.idiomatic: Without preaching they transformed those around them; heaven and humanity responded in kind.

sentences.zh: 雖或位登臺輔，爵列王侯，祿積萬鐘，馬跡千駟，死之日曾不得與斯人之徒隸齒。

translations.literal: Even if some rose to the rank of chief minister, were enfeoffed as kings or marquises, amassed stipends of ten thousand piculs, and left the tracks of a thousand teams of horses, on the day of their death they could not even be ranked with the servants of such men as these.
translations.idiomatic: Even those who reached the highest councils of state, held princely titles, piled up stipends by the ten thousand piculs, and rode out with a thousand teams of horses—in death they could not stand even with the household retainers of these filial sons.

sentences.zh: 孝之大也，不其然乎。

translations.literal: How great filial piety is—is it not indeed so!
translations.idiomatic: Such is the greatness of filial piety—is it not exactly so?

sentences.zh: 案《魏書》列趙琰、長孫慮、乞伏保、孫益德、董洛生、楊引、閻元明、吳悉達、王續生、李顯達、倉跋、張升、王崇、郭文恭為《孝感傳》，《周書》列李棠、柳檜、杜叔毗、荊可、秦族、皇甫遐、張元為《孝義傳》，《隋書》列陸彥師、田德懋、薛浚、王頒、田翼、楊慶、郭世俊、紐因、劉仕俊、郎方貴、翟普林、李德饒、華秋、徐孝肅為《孝義傳》。

translations.literal: According to the History of Wei, Zhao Yan, Zhangsun Lü, Qifu Bao, Sun Yide, Dong Luosheng, Yang Yin, Yan Yuanming, Wu Xida, Wang Xusheng, Li Xianda, Cang Ba, Zhang Sheng, Wang Chong, and Guo Wengong were entered in the "Biographies of Filial Response"; the History of Zhou entered Li Tang, Liu Gui, Du Shupi, Jing Ke, Qin Zu, Huangfu Xia, and Zhang Yuan in the "Biographies of Filial Righteousness"; the History of Sui entered Lu Yanshi, Tian Demao, Xue Jun, Wang Ban, Tian Yi, Yang Qing, Guo Shijun, Niu Yin, Liu Shijun, Lang Fanggui, Zhai Pulü, Li Derao, Hua Qiu, and Xu Xiaosu in the "Biographies of Filial Righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: The History of Wei placed Zhao Yan, Zhangsun Lü, Qifu Bao, Sun Yide, Dong Luosheng, Yang Yin, Yan Yuanming, Wu Xida, Wang Xusheng, Li Xianda, Cang Ba, Zhang Sheng, Wang Chong, and Guo Wengong in its "Biographies of Filial Response"; the History of Zhou placed Li Tang, Liu Gui, Du Shupi, Jing Ke, Qin Zu, Huangfu Xia, and Zhang Yuan in its "Biographies of Filial Righteousness"; and the History of Sui placed Lu Yanshi, Tian Demao, Xue Jun, Wang Ban, Tian Yi, Yang Qing, Guo Shijun, Niu Yin, Liu Shijun, Lang Fanggui, Zhai Pulü, Li Derao, Hua Qiu, and Xu Xiaosu in its "Biographies of Filial Righteousness."

sentences.zh: 今趙琰、李棠、柳檜、杜叔毗、陵彥師、李德饒入別傳及其家傳，其餘並從此編緝，以備《孝行傳》云。

translations.literal: Now Zhao Yan, Li Tang, Liu Gui, Du Shupi, Lu Yanshi, and Li Derao have been placed in separate biographies and their family histories; the rest are all compiled here to complete this "Biographies of Filial Conduct."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan, Li Tang, Liu Gui, Du Shupi, Lu Yanshi, and Li Derao now appear in separate biographies and family histories; the remainder are gathered here to form this "Biographies of Filial Conduct."

sentences.zh: 長孫慮，代人也。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Lü was a native of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Lü came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 母因飲酒，其父真呵叱之，誤以杖擊，便即致死。

translations.literal: His mother, because of drinking wine, was scolded by his father Zhen, who in error struck her with a staff and immediately killed her.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had been drinking; his father Zhen rebuked her and, mistaking his aim, struck her with a staff and killed her on the spot.

sentences.zh: 真為縣囚執，處以重坐。

translations.literal: Zhen was seized and imprisoned by the county and sentenced to a heavy penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was arrested by the county authorities and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 慮列辭尚書云：「父母忿爭，本無餘惡，直以謬誤，一朝橫禍。

translations.literal: Lü submitted a memorial to the Imperial Secretariat, saying: "When parents quarrel in anger, there is originally no further malice; it was solely through a mistaken blow that sudden calamity struck in a single morning."
translations.idiomatic: Lü submitted a petition to the Imperial Secretariat: "When parents quarrel in anger, there is no deeper malice—only a mistaken blow that brought sudden disaster in a single morning."

sentences.zh: 今母喪未殯，父命旦夕，慮兄弟五人並沖幼。

translations.literal: "Now my mother's funeral is not yet complete, and my father's life hangs by the day; Lü and his five brothers are all still young."
translations.idiomatic: "My mother's body has not yet been buried, and my father's life hangs by a thread; I and my five brothers are all still young."

sentences.zh: 慮身居長，今年十五，有一女弟，向始四歲。

translations.literal: "Lü, as the eldest, is fifteen this year; there is one younger sister who has only just turned four."
translations.idiomatic: "As the eldest son I am fifteen; I have one younger sister who has only just turned four."

sentences.zh: 更相鞠養，不能保全，父若就刑，交墜溝壑。

translations.literal: "If we take turns nurturing one another, we cannot preserve ourselves; if father goes to execution, we will all fall together into ditch and gully."
translations.idiomatic: "If we must raise one another, we cannot survive; if father is executed, we shall all perish together."

sentences.zh: 乞以身代老父命，使嬰弱眾孤，得蒙存立。

translations.literal: "I beg to offer my body in place of my aged father's life, so that these infants, the weak, and the many orphans may receive preservation and standing."
translations.idiomatic: "I beg to die in my aged father's place, so that these infants and helpless orphans may be allowed to live."

sentences.zh: 」尚書奏云：「慮于父為孝子，于弟為仁兄，尋情究狀，特可矜感。

translations.literal: The Secretariat memorialized: "Toward his father Lü is a filial son; toward his younger brothers he is a benevolent elder brother. Investigating the feelings and examining the facts, he is especially worthy of compassion and admiration."
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat reported: "Toward his father Lü is a filial son; toward his brothers he is a benevolent elder sibling. Weighing the circumstances, his case is especially moving and deserving of mercy."

sentences.zh: 」孝文帝詔特恕其父死罪，以從遠流。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen of Wei issued an edict specially pardoning his father's capital crime and commuting him to exile to a distant region.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict specially sparing his father's life and sentencing him to exile in a distant region instead.

sentences.zh: 乞伏保，高車部人也。

translations.literal: Qifu Bao was a man of the Gaoche tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Bao belonged to the Gaoche people.

sentences.zh: 父居，獻文時為散騎常侍，領牧曹尚書，賜爵甯國侯。

translations.literal: His father Ju, in the time of Emperor Xianwen, served as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrently as Director of the Pasturage Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ju, under Emperor Xianwen, served as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrently as Director of the Pasturage Bureau, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ning.

sentences.zh: 以忠謹慎密，常在左右，出內詔命。

translations.literal: Because of his loyalty, prudence, and discretion he was constantly at the emperor's side, issuing and receiving imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Trusted for his loyalty, prudence, and discretion, he remained constantly at the emperor's side, conveying edicts in and out of the palace.

sentences.zh: 賜宮人河南宗氏，亡後，賜以宮人申氏，宋太子左率申坦兄女也。

translations.literal: He was granted the palace woman Zong of Henan; after her death he was granted the palace woman Lady Shen, daughter of the elder brother of Shen Tan, Left Commander of the Crown Prince's Guard of Song.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him the palace woman Zong of Henan; after she died, he received the palace woman Lady Shen, niece of Shen Tan, Left Commander of the Crown Prince's Guard of Song.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，居卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Ju died.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later, Ju died.

sentences.zh: 申撫養伏保，性嚴肅，捶罵切至，而伏保奉事孝謹，初無恨色。

translations.literal: Shen reared and nurtured Bao; her nature was stern and severe, and her beatings and scoldings were harsh to the utmost, yet Bao served her with filial care and at first showed no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Shen raised Bao herself. Stern by nature, she beat and scolded him harshly, yet Bao served her with filial devotion and never once showed resentment.

sentences.zh: 襲父侯爵，例降為伯。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's marquisate, which by regulation was reduced to a barony.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's marquisate, which by regulation was reduced to a barony.

sentences.zh: 稍遷左中郎將。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Left Commandant of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually promoted to Left Commandant of the Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 每請祿賜，在外公私尺丈所用，無不白知。

translations.literal: Whenever he requested salary or gifts, whatever was used in public or private affairs abroad, down to every foot and inch, he reported without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he drew salary or gifts, he reported every item used in his public and private affairs abroad, down to the last measure.

sentences.zh: 出為鄯善鎮將。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Garrison Commander of Shanshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Garrison Commander of Shanshan.

sentences.zh: 申年逾八十，伏保手制馬車，親自扶接，申欣然隨之。

translations.literal: When Shen passed eighty years, Bao personally built a horse carriage with his own hands and himself supported and received her; Shen followed gladly.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen passed eighty, Bao built a carriage with his own hands and personally helped her aboard; she followed him gladly.

sentences.zh: 申亡，伏保解官，奉喪還洛。

translations.literal: When Shen died, Bao resigned his office and escorted the coffin back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen died, Bao resigned his post and escorted her coffin back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 復為長兼南中郎將，卒。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Acting Chief and Concurrent Southern Commandant of the Palace Guards, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed Acting Chief and Concurrent Southern Commandant of the Palace Guards, and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 孫益德，樂安人也。

translations.literal: Sun Yide was a native of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yide came from Le'an.

sentences.zh: 其母為人所害。

translations.literal: His mother was killed by someone.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was murdered.

sentences.zh: 益德童幼，為母復仇，還家哭於殯，以待縣官。

translations.literal: Yide, though still a child, avenged his mother, returned home to weep beside the bier, and waited for the county authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Though still a child, Yide avenged his mother, returned home to mourn beside her bier, and waited for the county magistrate to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 孝文、文明太后以其幼而孝決，又不逃罪，特免之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming, because he was young yet resolute in filial piety and did not flee punishment, specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming, moved that one so young could be so resolute in filial duty and did not flee justice, specially pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 董洛生，代人也。

translations.literal: Dong Luosheng was a native of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Luosheng came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 居父喪過禮，詔遣秘書中散溫紹伯奉璽書慰之，令自抑割，以全孝道。

translations.literal: In observing mourning for his father he exceeded the rites; an edict dispatched Secretariat Attendant Wen Shaobo bearing an imperial letter of consolation, ordering him to restrain himself so as to preserve the fullness of filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His mourning for his father exceeded the proper bounds; the throne sent Secretariat Attendant Wen Shaobo with an imperial letter of consolation, urging him to restrain his grief so as to fulfill filial duty in the proper way.

sentences.zh: 又詔其宗親，使相喻獎，勿令有滅性之譏。

translations.literal: The throne also ordered his kinsmen to admonish and encourage him in turn, lest he incur reproach for destroying his own life.
translations.idiomatic: The throne also ordered his kinsmen to counsel and encourage him, lest he bring upon himself the reproach of sacrificing his life to grief.

sentences.zh: 楊引，鄉郡襄垣人也。

translations.literal: Yang Yin was a native of Xiangyuan in Xiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin came from Xiangyuan in Xiang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 三歲喪父，為叔所養。

translations.literal: He lost his father at three and was reared by his uncle.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at the age of three and was raised by his uncle.

sentences.zh: 母年九十二終，引年七十五，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: His mother died at ninety-two; Yin was seventy-five, and his grief and emaciation exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died at ninety-two, Yin was seventy-five; his mourning exceeded all proper bounds.

sentences.zh: 三年服畢，恨不識父，追服斬衰，食粥粗服，誓終身命。

translations.literal: When the three-year mourning was complete, grieving that he had never known his father, he put on the hemmed sackcloth of the most severe mourning, ate only gruel, wore only coarse garments, and vowed it for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: When the three-year mourning for his mother ended, grieving that he had never known his father, he donned the severest mourning garb, ate only gruel, wore only coarse cloth, and vowed to continue for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 經十三年，哀慕不改，為郡縣鄉閭三百餘人上狀稱美。

translations.literal: After thirteen years his grief and longing were unchanged; more than three hundred people of the commandery, county, and village submitted memorials praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen years passed and his grief never wavered; more than three hundred people from his commandery, county, and village submitted memorials praising his conduct.

sentences.zh: 有司奏宜旌賞，復其一門，樹其純孝。

translations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized that he ought to be commended and rewarded, that his entire household be exempted from levies, and that his pure filial piety be made a model.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices recommended that he be honored and rewarded, that his entire household be exempted from taxes and corvée, and that his pure filial devotion be held up as an example.

sentences.zh: 詔別敕集書標揚引至行，又可假以散員之名。

translations.literal: An edict specially ordered the Imperial Secretariat to proclaim and praise Yin's utmost conduct, and further granted him an honorary title as a supernumerary official.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Imperial Secretariat to proclaim Yin's exemplary conduct, and granted him an honorary supernumerary title as well.

sentences.zh: 閻元明，河東安邑人也。

translations.literal: Yan Yuanming was a native of Anyi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yuanming came from Anyi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 少而至孝，行著鄉閭。

translations.literal: From youth he was utterly filial, and his conduct was renowned in his village.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was profoundly filial, and his conduct was renowned throughout his village.

sentences.zh: 太和五年，除北隨郡太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe he was appointed Administrator of Beisui Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taihe he was appointed Administrator of Beisui Commandery.

sentences.zh: 元明以違離親養，興言悲慕。

translations.literal: Yuanming, because he was separated from nurturing his parents, spoke with grief and longing.
translations.idiomatic: Separated from his parents, Yuanming spoke constantly of grief and longing.

sentences.zh: 母亦慈念，泣淚喪明。

translations.literal: His mother likewise cherished him in her thoughts, weeping until her tears blinded her.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, longing for him in turn, wept until she lost her sight.

sentences.zh: 悲號上訴，許歸奉養。

translations.literal: He wailed and appealed upward; permission was granted to return and support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He appealed in grief to the throne and was permitted to return home to care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 一見其母，母目便開。

translations.literal: As soon as he saw his mother, her eyes at once opened again.
translations.idiomatic: The moment he saw his mother, her eyes opened again.

sentences.zh: 刺史呂壽恩列狀上聞，詔下州郡，表為孝門，復其租調兵役，令終母年。

translations.literal: Inspector Lü Shou'en submitted a detailed report to the throne; an edict went down to the provinces and commanderies, designating his household a Gate of Filial Piety, exempting them from land tax and corvée, and ordering that he remain until his mother's years were complete.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Lü Shou'en reported the matter to the throne; an edict went out to the provinces designating the household a Gate of Filial Piety, exempting it from taxes and corvée, and permitting Yuanming to remain at home until his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 母亡服終，心喪積載，每忌日，悲動傍鄰。

translations.literal: After his mother died and the mourning period ended, his inner grief accumulated for years; on each anniversary of her death his sorrow moved the neighbors beside him.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died and the formal mourning ended, his inner grief endured for years; on each anniversary his sorrow moved the neighbors around him.

sentences.zh: 昆弟雍和，尊卑諧穆，安貧樂道，白首同歸。

translations.literal: Brothers were harmonious, elders and juniors amicable; content in poverty and devoted to the Way, they shared the same path to white-haired old age.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers lived in harmony, elders and juniors in mutual respect; content in poverty and devoted to virtue, they walked the same path into old age.

sentences.zh: 又猗氏縣人令狐仕，兄弟四人，早喪父，泣慕十載，奉養其母，孝著鄉邑。

translations.literal: Moreover, Linghu Shi of Yishi County—four brothers who early lost their father—wept and yearned for ten years, supported their mother, and were famed for filial piety in village and town.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Linghu Shi of Yishi County: four brothers who lost their father early, mourned him for ten years, supported their mother, and won renown for filial piety throughout their district.

sentences.zh: 而力田積粟，博施不已。

translations.literal: They labored in the fields and amassed grain, giving generously without cease.
translations.idiomatic: They worked the fields tirelessly, stored grain, and gave generously without end.

sentences.zh: 又河東郡人楊風等七百五十人，列稱樂戶皇甫奴兄弟，雖沉屈兵伍，而操尚彌高，奉養繼親，甚著恭孝之稱。

translations.literal: Moreover, Yang Feng and seven hundred fifty others of Hedong Commandery jointly reported that the brothers Huangfu Nu of the music-house register, though sunk low in the ranks of soldiery, maintained conduct still higher, supporting their stepmother and winning great renown for respectful filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred fifty people of Hedong Commandery, led by Yang Feng, jointly reported that the brothers Huangfu Nu—registered musicians though they were, and sunk low in the army ranks—conducted themselves with exceptional dignity, supported their stepmother, and were widely praised for respectful filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 又東郡小黃縣人董吐渾、兄養，事親至孝，三世同居，閨門有禮。

translations.literal: Moreover, Dong Tuhun and his elder brother Yang of Xiaohuang County in Dong Commandery served their parents with utmost filial piety; three generations dwelt together and the inner gates observed ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Tuhun and his elder brother Yang of Xiaohuang County in Dong Commandery also served their parents with the utmost filial devotion; three generations lived under one roof, and their household was a model of ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 景明初，畿內大使王凝奏請標異，詔從之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingming era, Metropolitan Envoy Wang Ning memorialized requesting that they be marked out for distinction; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingming era, Metropolitan Envoy Wang Ning recommended them for special recognition, and the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 吳悉達，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Wu Xida was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xida came from Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 兄弟三人，年並幼小，父母為人所殺。

translations.literal: Three brothers, all still young in years, whose parents were killed by others.
translations.idiomatic: Three brothers, all still young, whose parents had been murdered.

sentences.zh: 四時號慕，悲感鄉鄰。

translations.literal: Through the four seasons they wailed and yearned, their grief moving the neighbors of the village.
translations.idiomatic: Season after season they wailed in grief, moving all their neighbors to sorrow.

sentences.zh: 及長報仇，避地永安。

translations.literal: When they grew up they took revenge and removed to Yong'an to avoid trouble.
translations.idiomatic: When they grew up they avenged their parents and moved to Yong'an to escape reprisals.

sentences.zh: 昆弟同居四十餘載，閨門和睦，讓逸競勞。

translations.literal: The brothers dwelt together for more than forty years; within the gates there was harmony, yielding ease and vying in labor.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers lived together for more than forty years in household harmony, each yielding comfort to the others and competing only in hard work.

sentences.zh: 雖於儉年，糊饘不繼，賓客經過，必傾所有。

translations.literal: Even in lean years when thin gruel could not be kept up, whenever guests passed by they would pour out all they possessed.
translations.idiomatic: Even in lean years when they could scarcely keep thin gruel on the table, any guest who passed by found them pouring out everything they had.

sentences.zh: 每守宰殯喪，私辦車牛，送終葬所。

translations.literal: Whenever a magistrate or administrator had a funeral, they privately provided carts and oxen to escort the coffin to the burial ground.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a local official died, they privately supplied carts and oxen to convey the coffin to the burial ground.

sentences.zh: 鄰人孤貧窘困者，莫不解衣輟糧，以相賑恤。

translations.literal: For neighbors who were orphaned, poor, or in desperate straits, there was none for whom they did not strip off garments or set aside grain to relieve and succor.
translations.idiomatic: For neighbors who were orphaned, destitute, or in desperate need, they always stripped off their own garments or set aside grain to help.

sentences.zh: 鄉閭五百餘人詣州稱頌焉。

translations.literal: More than five hundred people of the village went to the province to praise them.
translations.idiomatic: More than five hundred villagers went to the provincial capital to praise their conduct.

sentences.zh: 刺史以悉達兄弟行著鄉里，板贈悉達父勃海太守。

translations.literal: The inspector, because the Xida brothers' conduct was renowned in their village, posthumously enfeoffed Xida's father as Administrator of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: The inspector, moved by the brothers' renown in their village, posthumously appointed Xida's father Administrator of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 悉達後欲改葬，亡失墳墓，推尋弗獲。

translations.literal: Later Xida wished to rebury his father, but the grave had been lost and could not be found despite searching.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xida wished to rebury his father, but the grave had been lost and could not be found despite every effort.

sentences.zh: 號哭之聲，晝夜不止，叫訴神祇。

translations.literal: The sound of his wailing did not cease day or night as he cried out to the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: His wailing never ceased, day or night, as he cried out to heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 忽于悉達足下地陷，得父銘記，因遷葬曾祖已下三世九喪。

translations.literal: Suddenly the ground sank beneath Xida's feet and he obtained his father's inscribed marker; he therefore moved the burials of nine coffins from the great-grandfather down through three generations.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly the ground sank beneath his feet and he found his father's inscribed marker; he then reburied nine coffins spanning three generations from his great-grandfather onward.

sentences.zh: 傾盡資業，不假於人，哀感毀悴，有過初喪。

translations.literal: He exhausted his entire estate without borrowing from others; his grief moved heaven and he wasted away, exceeding even his first mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his entire estate without borrowing from anyone; his grief was so profound that he wasted away, more deeply than even at his first mourning.

sentences.zh: 有司奏聞，標閭復役，以彰孝義。

translations.literal: The responsible officials reported to the throne, marked his lane, and restored him from corvée labor, in order to proclaim filial righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities submitted a memorial to the throne; his household lane was marked with an honorific sign and he was exempted from corvée labor to proclaim his filial devotion and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 時有齊州人崔承宗，其父于宋世仕漢中，母喪因殯彼。

translations.literal: At that time there was Cui Chengzong of Qi Province; his father during the Song dynasty had served in Hanzhong, and when his mother died she was provisionally entombed there.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was a man of Qi Province named Cui Chengzong. His father had served in Hanzhong during the Song dynasty, and when his mother died she was temporarily buried there.

sentences.zh: 後青、徐歸魏，遂為隔絕。

translations.literal: Later Qing and Xu returned to Wei, and thus they were cut off from each other.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Qing and Xu came under Wei rule, the family was cut off from the mother's grave.

sentences.zh: 承宗性至孝，萬里投險，偷路負喪還京師。

translations.literal: Chengzong was by nature supremely filial; he traveled ten thousand li through danger, taking secret paths to carry the coffin back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong was supremely filial by nature. He traveled ten thousand li through perilous country, finding secret routes to carry his mother's coffin back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎孫惠蔚聞之，曰：「吾於斯人，見廉範之情矣。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Attendant Sun Huiwei heard of it and said: "In this man I see the sentiment of Lian and Fan."
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Attendant Sun Huiwei heard of it and said, "In this man I see the devotion of Lian and Fan."

sentences.zh: 」於是吊贈盡禮，如舊相識。

translations.literal: Thereupon he paid his respects at the funeral and made gifts with full propriety, as if to an old acquaintance.
translations.idiomatic: He then offered full funeral condolences and gifts, treating Chengzong as though they were old friends.

sentences.zh: 王續生，滎陽京縣人也。

translations.literal: Wang Xusheng was a native of Jing County in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xusheng came from Jing County in Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 遭繼母憂，居喪，杖而後起。

translations.literal: He suffered the bereavement of his stepmother; during mourning he could rise only with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: When his stepmother died, he entered mourning and was so weakened that he could rise only with the help of a staff.

sentences.zh: 乃終禮制，鬢髮盡落。

translations.literal: When the mourning rites were finally completed, all the hair at his temples had fallen out.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the mourning period ended, all the hair at his temples had fallen out.

sentences.zh: 有司奏聞，宣武詔標旌門閭，甄其徭役。

translations.literal: The authorities reported to the throne; Emperor Xuanwu decreed that his gate and lane be marked with honorific banners and that his corvée labor be waived.
translations.idiomatic: The officials reported the matter to the throne, and Emperor Xuanwu decreed that Wang's gate and lane be marked with an honorific banner and that he be exempted from corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 李顯達，潁川陽翟人也。

translations.literal: Li Xianda was a native of Yangzhai in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianda came from Yangzhai in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 父喪，水漿不入口七日，鬢髮墮落，形體枯悴。

translations.literal: At his father's death he took neither water nor gruel for seven days; the hair at his temples fell out and his body withered away.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he took neither water nor food for seven days. The hair at his temples fell out and his body wasted away.

sentences.zh: 六年廬於墓側，哭不絕聲，殆於滅性。

translations.literal: For six years he lived in a hut beside the tomb, weeping without cease, nearly destroying his life.
translations.idiomatic: For six years he lived in a hut beside the tomb, weeping without cease until he nearly destroyed himself with grief.

sentences.zh: 州牧高陽王雍以狀奏，靈太后詔表其門閭。

translations.literal: The provincial governor, the Prince of Gaoyang Yong, submitted a report on his case; Empress Dowager Ling decreed that his gate and lane be marked with honor.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial governor, Prince Yong of Gaoyang, submitted a report on his case, and Empress Dowager Ling decreed that his gate and lane be marked with honor.

sentences.zh: 倉跋，滎陽京縣人也。

translations.literal: Cang Ba was a native of Jing County in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cang Ba came from Jing County in Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 喪母，水漿不入口五日，吐血數升，居憂毀瘠，見稱州裏。

translations.literal: When his mother died he took neither water nor gruel for five days, vomited several sheng of blood, wasted away in grief, and was praised throughout the province.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he took neither water nor food for five days, vomited several sheng of blood, and wasted away in grief until he was praised throughout the province.

sentences.zh: 有司奏聞，孝武帝詔標門閭。

translations.literal: The authorities reported to the throne; Emperor Xiaowu decreed that his gate and lane be marked with honor.
translations.idiomatic: The officials reported the matter to the throne, and Emperor Xiaowu decreed that his gate and lane be marked with honor.

sentences.zh: 張升，滎陽京縣人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Sheng was a native of Jing County in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheng came from Jing County in Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 喪父，飲水絕鹽，哀毀過度，形骸枯悴，骨立而已，發落殆盡。

translations.literal: When his father died he drank water but took no salt; his grief and self-destruction were excessive—his frame withered until only his bones stood out, and his hair nearly all fell out.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he drank water but took no salt. His grief was so extreme that his body wasted away to skin and bone and his hair nearly all fell out.

sentences.zh: 聲聞鄉里，盜賊不侵其閭。

translations.literal: His renown spread through the village, and bandits did not harass his lane.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation spread through the countryside, and even bandits would not disturb his household lane.

sentences.zh: 州表以聞，標其門閭。

translations.literal: The province submitted a report to the throne, and his gate and lane were marked with honor.
translations.idiomatic: The province submitted a report to the throne, and his gate and lane were marked with honor.

sentences.zh: 王崇，字乾邕，陽夏雍人也。

translations.literal: Wang Chong, courtesy name Qianyou, was a native of Yong in Yangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chong, courtesy name Qianyou, came from Yong in Yangxia.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並以孝稱，身勤稼穡，以養二親。

translations.literal: The brothers were all known for filial piety; he personally worked hard at farming to support both parents.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were all known for filial piety. Wang Chong personally worked hard in the fields to support both his parents.

sentences.zh: 仕梁州鎮南府主簿。

translations.literal: He served as principal clerk in the Southern Garrison office of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as principal clerk in the Southern Garrison headquarters of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 母亡，杖而後起，鬢髮墮落。

translations.literal: When his mother died he could rise only with a staff, and the hair at his temples fell out.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he was so weakened that he could rise only with a staff, and the hair at his temples fell out.

sentences.zh: 未及葬，權殯宅西。

translations.literal: Before she could be buried, her body was provisionally entombed west of the house.
translations.idiomatic: Before she could be properly buried, her body was temporarily interred west of the house.

sentences.zh: 崇廬於殯所，晝夜哭泣，鳩鴿群至。

translations.literal: Chong built a hut at the temporary burial place and wept day and night; doves and pigeons came in flocks.
translations.idiomatic: Chong built a mourning hut beside the temporary tomb and wept day and night, and flocks of doves and pigeons gathered there.

sentences.zh: 有一小鳥，素質黑眸，形大於雀，棲於崇廬，朝夕不去。

translations.literal: There was one small bird, white in body with black eyes, larger than a sparrow; it roosted on Chong's hut and did not leave morning or evening.
translations.idiomatic: One small bird, white-bodied with black eyes and larger than a sparrow, roosted on Chong's hut and would not leave from morning to evening.

sentences.zh: 母喪闋，復丁父憂，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: When his mourning for his mother ended, he again suffered his father's bereavement; his grief and self-destruction exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning for his mother ended, his father died as well, and his grief exceeded what the rites prescribed.

sentences.zh: 是年夏，風雹，所經處，禽獸暴死，草木摧折。

translations.literal: That summer there was wind and hail; wherever it passed, birds and beasts died suddenly and plants and trees were snapped.
translations.idiomatic: That summer a storm of wind and hail swept through the land. Wherever it passed, birds and beasts died suddenly and plants and trees were broken.

sentences.zh: 至崇田畔，風雹便止，禾麥十頃，竟無損落。

translations.literal: When it reached the edge of Chong's fields, the wind and hail stopped at once—ten qing of grain and wheat suffered no damage at all.
translations.idiomatic: When the storm reached the edge of Chong's fields, the wind and hail stopped at once, and ten qing of grain and wheat were left completely undamaged.

sentences.zh: 及過崇地，風雹如初。

translations.literal: After passing beyond Chong's land, the wind and hail resumed as before.
translations.idiomatic: Once it had passed beyond Chong's land, the wind and hail resumed with the same fury as before.

sentences.zh: 咸稱至行所感。

translations.literal: All said it was moved by his supreme conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone said that heaven itself had been moved by his supreme filial conduct.

sentences.zh: 崇雖除服，仍居墓側。

translations.literal: Although Chong had ended mourning dress, he still lived beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Although Chong had completed the mourning period and put aside mourning dress, he still lived beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 於其室前，生草一根，莖葉甚茂，人莫能識。

translations.literal: Before his hut a single stalk of grass grew, its stem and leaves very lush; no one could identify it.
translations.idiomatic: Before his hut a single stalk of grass sprang up, its stem and leaves unusually lush, though no one could identify the species.

sentences.zh: 至冬中，復有鳥巢崇屋，乳養三子，毛羽成長，馴而不驚。

translations.literal: By midwinter birds again nested on Chong's dwelling, nursed three young, their feathers matured, tame and unafraid.
translations.idiomatic: By midwinter birds nested again on Chong's hut, raised three chicks until their feathers were fully grown, tame and unafraid of people.

sentences.zh: 守令聞之，親自臨視。

translations.literal: The district magistrate heard of it and came in person to look.
translations.idiomatic: When the district magistrate heard of it, he came in person to see for himself.

sentences.zh: 州以聞奏，標其門閭。

translations.literal: The province reported it to the throne, and his gate and lane were marked with honor.
translations.idiomatic: The province reported the matter to the throne, and his gate and lane were marked with honor.

sentences.zh: 郭文恭，太原平遙人也。

translations.literal: Guo Wengong was a native of Pingyao in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wengong came from Pingyao in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 仕為太平縣令。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Taiping County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Taiping County.

sentences.zh: 年逾七十，父母喪亡。

translations.literal: Past the age of seventy, his parents died.
translations.idiomatic: After he had passed seventy, both his parents died.

sentences.zh: 文恭孝慕罔極，乃居祖父墓次，晨夕拜跪。

translations.literal: Wengong's filial longing was boundless; he therefore lived at his grandfather's tomb mound, bowing and kneeling morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Wengong's filial longing knew no bounds. He lived at his grandfather's tomb mound, bowing and kneeling morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 跣足負土，培祖父二墓，寒暑竭力，積年不已。

translations.literal: Barefoot he carried earth to mound his grandfather's two graves, striving through cold and heat without cease for years on end.
translations.idiomatic: Barefoot, he carried earth to build up his grandfather's two graves, laboring through heat and cold year after year without rest.

sentences.zh: 見者莫不哀歎。

translations.literal: Those who saw him none failed to mourn and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: All who saw him were moved to grief and sighing.

sentences.zh: 尚書聞奏，標其門閭。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Works heard and reported it; his gate and lane were marked with honor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Works learned of it and reported the matter, his gate and lane were marked with honor.

sentences.zh: 荊可，河東猗氏人也。

translations.literal: Jing Ke was a native of Yishi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Ke came from Yishi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 性質樸，容止有異於人。

translations.literal: His nature was simple and unadorned; his bearing differed from ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was plain and unadorned, and his bearing set him apart from other men.

sentences.zh: 能苦身勤力，供養其母，隨時甘旨，終無匱乏。

translations.literal: He could afflict his body and exert himself, supporting his mother with delicacies according to the season—never a shortage.
translations.idiomatic: He endured hardship and toiled tirelessly to support his mother, providing seasonal delicacies without ever falling short.

sentences.zh: 母喪，水漿不入口三日，悲號擗踴，絕而後蘇者數四。

translations.literal: At his mother's death he took neither water nor gruel for three days, wailing and beating his breast; he lost consciousness and came back to life several times.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he took neither water nor food for three days, wailing and beating his breast until he fainted and revived several times over.

sentences.zh: 葬母之後，遂廬於墓側，晝夜悲哭，負土成墳，蓬發不櫛，菜食飲水而已。

translations.literal: After burying his mother he built a hut beside the tomb, weeping in grief day and night, carrying earth to form the mound, his tangled hair uncombed, eating vegetables and drinking water only.
translations.idiomatic: After burying his mother, he built a hut beside the tomb and wept day and night. He carried earth to build up the mound, left his tangled hair uncombed, and ate nothing but vegetables and water.

sentences.zh: 然可家舊墓，塋域極大，榛蕪至深，去家十餘里。

translations.literal: Yet the Ke family's old cemetery was very large, overgrown with deep brambles and weeds, more than ten li from home.
translations.idiomatic: The Ke family's old cemetery, however, was vast and deeply overgrown with brambles and weeds, more than ten li from his home.

sentences.zh: 而可獨宿其中，與禽獸雜處，哀感遠近，邑裏稱之。

translations.literal: Yet Ke alone lodged within it, mingling with wild beasts; his grief moved those near and far, and the town praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ke slept there alone among the wild beasts. His grief moved people near and far, and the whole town praised him.

sentences.zh: 大統中，可鄉人以可孝行足以勸勵風俗，乃上言焉。

translations.literal: During Datong, Ke's fellow townsmen, holding that his filial conduct could encourage and reform custom, submitted a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: During the Datong era, Ke's fellow townsmen submitted a memorial, saying that his filial conduct was sufficient to encourage and reform public morals.

sentences.zh: 周文令州縣表異之。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen ordered the province and counties to report his exceptional virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen ordered the provincial and county authorities to report Ke's exceptional virtue to the throne.

sentences.zh: 及服終之後，猶若居喪。

translations.literal: After the mourning period ended, he still acted as if in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the mourning period ended, he continued to live as though still in mourning.

sentences.zh: 大塚宰、晉公護聞可孝行，特引見焉。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of State, Duke of Jin Hu heard of Ke's filial conduct and specially summoned him for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of State Hu, Duke of Jin, heard of Ke's filial conduct and specially summoned him for an audience.

sentences.zh: 與可言論，時有會於護意。

translations.literal: He conversed with Ke, and at times their thoughts accorded with Hu's intentions.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke with Ke, and at times Ke's words accorded perfectly with Hu's own thoughts.

sentences.zh: 而護亦至孝，其母閻氏，沒於敵境，不測存亡。

translations.literal: Hu was also supremely filial; his mother Lady Yan had perished in enemy territory, her fate unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Hu was also supremely filial. His mother, Lady Yan, had died in enemy territory, and no one knew whether she was alive or dead.

sentences.zh: 每見可，自傷久乖膝下，而重可至性。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw Ke, he grieved that he had long been parted from his mother's presence, and he esteemed Ke's supreme filial nature.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Hu saw Ke, he grieved that he had long been parted from his mother's side, and he deeply admired Ke's supreme filial nature.

sentences.zh: 可卒後，護猶思其純孝，收可妻子于京城，恆給其衣食。

translations.literal: After Ke's death, Hu still thought of his pure filial devotion, took in Ke's wife and children in the capital, and constantly provided them with food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: After Ke died, Hu still remembered his pure filial devotion. He took in Ke's wife and children in the capital and constantly provided for their food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 秦族，上郡洛川人也。

translations.literal: Qin Zu was a native of Luochuan in Shang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zu came from Luochuan in Shang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖白、父雚，並有至性，聞於閭里。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bai and father Guan both had supreme natures, renowned in the neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bai and his father Guan both possessed exceptional moral character and were renowned in their neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 魏太和中，板白潁州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Wei dynasty's Taihe era, Bai was appointed by edict as governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era of the Wei dynasty, Bai was appointed by edict as governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 大統中，板雚酈城郡守。

translations.literal: In the Datong era, Guan was appointed by edict as prefect of Licheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Datong era, Guan was appointed by edict as prefect of Licheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 族性至孝，事親竭力。

translations.literal: Zu was supremely filial by nature and served his parents with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Zu was supremely filial by nature and served his parents with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 及父喪，哀毀過禮，每一慟哭，酸感行路。

translations.literal: When his father died his grief and self-destruction exceeded the rites; each time he wailed, passersby were moved to bitter sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, his grief exceeded what the rites prescribed, and each time he wailed passersby were moved to bitter sorrow.

sentences.zh: 既以母在，恆抑割哀情，以慰其母意。

translations.literal: Since his mother was still alive, he constantly restrained and cut short his grief to comfort her mind.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was still alive, he constantly restrained his grief in order to comfort her.

sentences.zh: 四時珍羞，未嘗匱乏。

translations.literal: Delicacies of all four seasons were never in want.
translations.idiomatic: Delicacies for all four seasons were never lacking.

sentences.zh: 與弟榮先，復相友愛，閨門之中，怡怡如也。

translations.literal: With his younger brother Rongxian he was also mutually affectionate; within the family gates all was harmonious and glad.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Rongxian were deeply affectionate toward each other, and harmony reigned within the household.

sentences.zh: 尋而其母又沒，哭泣無時，唯飲水食菜而已。

translations.literal: Soon after his mother also died; he wept at no fixed times, eating only vegetables and drinking water.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his mother also died. He wept at all hours and ate nothing but vegetables and water.

sentences.zh: 終喪之後，猶蔬食，不入房室二十許年。

translations.literal: After mourning ended he still ate only vegetables and did not enter the bedchamber for some twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period ended, he continued to eat only vegetables and did not enter the marital bedchamber for some twenty years.

sentences.zh: 鄉里咸歎異之。

translations.literal: The neighborhood all marvelled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the neighborhood marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 其邑人王元達等七十餘人上其狀，有詔表其門閭。

translations.literal: More than seventy of his fellow townsmen including Wang Yuanda submitted a report on his case; an imperial decree marked his gate and lane with honor.
translations.idiomatic: More than seventy of his fellow townsmen, including Wang Yuanda, submitted a report on his case, and an imperial decree marked his gate and lane with honor.

sentences.zh: 榮先亦至孝，遭父喪，哀慕不已，遂以毀卒。

translations.literal: Rongxian was also supremely filial; when his father died his grief and longing did not cease, and he ultimately died from self-destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Rongxian was also supremely filial. When his father died, his grief and longing never ceased, and he ultimately died from the damage he had done to himself.

sentences.zh: 邑裏化其孝行。

translations.literal: The town and neighborhood were transformed by his filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The whole town and neighborhood were moved and transformed by his filial conduct.

sentences.zh: 周文嘉之，乃下詔褒美其行，贈滄州刺史，以旌厥異。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen praised him, issued an edict commending his conduct, posthumously awarded him Governor of Cangzhou, to proclaim his extraordinary virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen praised him, issued an edict commending his conduct, and posthumously appointed him Governor of Cangzhou to proclaim his extraordinary virtue.

sentences.zh: 皇甫遐，字永賢，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Huangfu Xia, courtesy name Yongxian, was a native of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Xia, courtesy name Yongxian, came from Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 累世寒微，而鄉里稱其和睦。

translations.literal: For generations his family had been poor and humble, yet the neighborhood praised their harmony.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had been poor and humble, yet the neighborhood praised their harmony.

sentences.zh: 遐性純至，少喪父，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Xia was pure and sincere by nature; he lost his father young and was known for serving his mother with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Xia was pure and sincere by nature. He lost his father at a young age and became known for serving his mother with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 後遭母喪，乃廬於墓側，負土為墳。

translations.literal: Later when his mother died he built a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to make the mound.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his mother died, he built a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build up the grave mound.

sentences.zh: 復于墓南作一禪窟，陰雨則穿窟，晴霽則營墓。

translations.literal: He also made a meditation cave south of the tomb—when it rained he worked in the cave, when the sky cleared he tended the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He also dug a meditation cave south of the tomb. When it rained he worked in the cave; when the sky cleared he tended the tomb.

sentences.zh: 曉夕勤力，未嘗暫停。

translations.literal: Morning and evening he toiled without ever pausing.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening he labored without ever resting.

sentences.zh: 積以歲年，墳高數丈，周回五十餘步，禪窟重台兩匝，總成十有二室，中間行道，可容百人。

translations.literal: Over years the mound rose several zhang, its circumference more than fifty paces; the meditation cave had two tiers stacked around, twelve chambers in all, with a path between that could hold a hundred people.
translations.idiomatic: Over the years the mound rose several zhang high and measured more than fifty paces around. The meditation cave had two stacked tiers with twelve chambers in all, and a central passage wide enough to hold a hundred people.

sentences.zh: 遐食粥枕塊，櫛風沐雨，形容枯悴，家人不識。

translations.literal: Xia ate gruel and slept on clods, exposed to wind and rain; his appearance withered so his family did not recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: Xia ate thin gruel and slept on clods of earth, enduring wind and rain until he was so gaunt that his own family no longer recognized him.

sentences.zh: 當其營墓之初，乃有鴟鳥各一，徘徊悲鳴，不離墓側，若助遐者，經月餘日乃去。

translations.literal: When he first began building the tomb, two owl-like birds appeared, circling and crying mournfully, never leaving the tomb side as if aiding Xia—after more than a month they departed.
translations.idiomatic: When he first began building the tomb, two owl-like birds appeared, circling and crying mournfully beside the grave as though helping him. They did not leave for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 遠近聞其至孝，競以米麵遺之，遐皆受而不食，悉以營佛齋焉。

translations.literal: Near and far heard of his supreme filial devotion and competed to bring him rice and flour; Xia accepted all but ate none, using everything for Buddhist offerings instead.
translations.idiomatic: People near and far heard of his supreme filial devotion and vied to bring him rice and flour. Xia accepted everything but ate none of it, using it all instead for Buddhist offerings.

sentences.zh: 郡縣表上其狀，有詔旌異之。

translations.literal: The commandery and county submitted reports on his case; an imperial decree proclaimed his exceptional virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery and county submitted reports on his case, and an imperial decree proclaimed his exceptional virtue.

sentences.zh: 張元，字孝始，河北芮城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuan, courtesy name Xiaoshi, was a native of Ruicheng in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuan, courtesy name Xiaoshi, came from Ruicheng in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 祖成，假平陽郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Cheng served as acting prefect of Pingyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Cheng served as acting prefect of Pingyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父延俊，仕州郡，累為功曹主簿。

translations.literal: His father Yanjun served in provincial and commandery offices, repeatedly as master of records clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanjun served in provincial and commandery offices, repeatedly holding posts such as master of records and principal clerk.

sentences.zh: 並以純至為鄉里所推。

translations.literal: Both were esteemed in the neighborhood for their pure sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Both were esteemed in the neighborhood for their pure and sincere character.

sentences.zh: 元性謙謹，有孝行，微涉經史，然精釋典。

translations.literal: Yuan was modest and careful by nature, with filial conduct; he lightly touched on the classics and histories but was deeply versed in Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was modest and careful by nature and known for filial conduct. He had some acquaintance with the classics and histories, but was deeply versed in Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 年六歲，其祖以其夏中熱，欲將元就井浴。

translations.literal: When he was six, his grandfather because of the summer heat wished to take Yuan to bathe at the well.
translations.idiomatic: When he was six years old, his grandfather, finding the midsummer heat unbearable, wanted to take Yuan to bathe at the well.

sentences.zh: 元固不肯從，謂其貪戲，乃以杖擊其頭曰：「汝何為不肯浴？

translations.literal: Yuan firmly refused; thinking him greedy for play, the grandfather struck his head with a staff and said: "Why will you not bathe?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan firmly refused. Thinking the boy was only trying to avoid bathing so he could keep playing, his grandfather struck him on the head with a staff and said, "Why will you not bathe?"

sentences.zh: 」元對曰：「衣以蓋形，為覆其褻。

translations.literal: Yuan replied: "Clothes are to cover the body, to conceal what is private."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan replied, "Clothes are meant to cover the body and conceal what is private."

sentences.zh: 元不能褻露其體于白日之下。

translations.literal: "Yuan cannot expose his naked body beneath the bright daylight."
translations.idiomatic: "I cannot expose my naked body in broad daylight."

sentences.zh: 」祖異而舍之。

translations.literal: The grandfather marveled and let him be.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was astonished and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 南鄰有二杏樹，杏熟多落元園中。

translations.literal: South of the house were two apricot trees; when the apricots ripened many fell into Yuan's garden.
translations.idiomatic: Two apricot trees stood south of the house, and when the fruit ripened many apricots fell into Yuan's garden.

sentences.zh: 諸小兒競取而食之。

translations.literal: The children all scrambled to take and eat them.
translations.idiomatic: The neighborhood children all scrambled to pick them up and eat them.

sentences.zh: 元所得者，送還其主。

translations.literal: What Yuan obtained he returned to the owner.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Yuan picked up, he returned to the trees' owner.

sentences.zh: 樹陌有狗子為人所棄者，元即收而養之。

translations.literal: On a tree-lined path there was a puppy that someone had abandoned; Yuan immediately took it in and raised it.
translations.idiomatic: On a tree-lined country path there was a puppy someone had cast away, and Yuan immediately took it in and cared for it.

sentences.zh: 其叔父怒曰：「何用此為！

translations.literal: His uncle said angrily, "What use is there in this!
translations.idiomatic: His uncle said in anger, "What good is this?"

sentences.zh: 」將欲更棄之。

translations.literal: " He was about to abandon it again.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to abandon the dog again.

sentences.zh: 元對曰：「有生之類，莫不重其性命。

translations.literal: Yuan replied, "Among living beings, there is none that does not value its life.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan replied, "Every living creature cherishes its own life."

sentences.zh: 若天生天殺，自然之理。

translations.literal: If Heaven gives life and Heaven takes it, that is the natural principle.
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven gives life and Heaven takes it away, that is the natural order of things.

sentences.zh: 今為人所棄而死，非其道也。

translations.literal: Now to die because one has been abandoned by people is not the proper way.
translations.idiomatic: But to die because people have cast you aside is not the way things should be.

sentences.zh: 若見而不收養，無仁心也。

translations.literal: If one sees this and does not take it in and raise it, one lacks a benevolent heart.
translations.idiomatic: If I see this and do not take the dog in, I would have no heart of human kindness.

sentences.zh: 是以收而養之。

translations.literal: Therefore I have taken it in and am raising it.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I have taken it in and am raising it.

sentences.zh: 」叔父感其言，遂許焉。

translations.literal: " His uncle was moved by his words and thereupon consented.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle was moved by what he said and agreed to let him keep the dog.

sentences.zh: 未幾，乃有狗母銜一死兔置元前而去。

translations.literal: Before long, a mother dog came carrying a dead rabbit in her mouth, placed it before Yuan, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, a mother dog appeared with a dead rabbit in her mouth, laid it before Yuan, and went away.

sentences.zh: 及元年十六，其祖喪明三年。

translations.literal: When Yuan reached sixteen, his grandfather had been blind for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan turned sixteen, his grandfather had already been blind for three years.

sentences.zh: 元恆憂泣，晝夜讀佛經，禮拜以祈福祐。

translations.literal: Yuan constantly grieved and wept, reading Buddhist scriptures day and night and performing obeisance to seek blessings and protection.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan wept in constant grief, reading Buddhist scriptures day and night and bowing in worship to seek divine blessing and protection.

sentences.zh: 後讀《藥師經》，見「盲者得視」之言。

translations.literal: Later, reading the Medicine Master Sutra, he saw the passage that says "the blind shall regain sight."
translations.idiomatic: Later he read the Bhaisajyaguru Sutra and came upon the passage saying, "the blind shall regain their sight."

sentences.zh: 遂請七僧，然七燈，七日七夜轉《藥師經》行道。

translations.literal: Thereupon he invited seven monks, lit seven lamps, and for seven days and seven nights performed circumambulatory recitation of the Medicine Master Sutra.
translations.idiomatic: He then invited seven monks, lit seven lamps, and for seven days and seven nights led a ritual circuit while reciting the Bhaisajyaguru Sutra.

sentences.zh: 每言：「天人師乎！

translations.literal: Each time he would say: "Teacher of gods and men!
translations.idiomatic: Each time he prayed, "Teacher of gods and men!

sentences.zh: 元為孫不孝，使祖喪明。

translations.literal: Yuan as a grandson has been unfilial, causing his grandfather to lose his sight.
translations.idiomatic: As your unworthy grandson, Yuan has failed in filial duty and caused my grandfather to lose his sight.

sentences.zh: 今以燈光普施法界，願祖目見明，元求代暗。

translations.literal: Now with lamp-light spread through all the dharma-realm, I pray that my grandfather's eyes may see clearly; Yuan asks to take the darkness in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Now by spreading this lamp-light through all the world, I pray that my grandfather's eyes may see clearly again, and I ask to bear the darkness in his place.

sentences.zh: 」如此經七日，其夜夢見一老翁，以金鑱療其祖目，於夢中喜躍，遂即驚覺。

translations.literal: After doing this for seven days, that night he dreamed of an old man using a golden awl to treat his grandfather's eyes; in the dream he leaped for joy, then startled awake.
translations.idiomatic: After seven days of this, that night he dreamed of an old man treating his grandfather's eyes with a golden awl. In the dream he leaped for joy, then woke with a start.

sentences.zh: 乃遍告家人。

translations.literal: He then told everyone in the household.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately told everyone in the household.

sentences.zh: 三日，祖目果明。

translations.literal: After three days, his grandfather's eyes indeed regained sight.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later, his grandfather's eyes truly regained their sight.

sentences.zh: 其後，祖臥疾再周，元恆隨祖所食多少，衣冠不解，旦夕扶侍。

translations.literal: Afterward, when his grandfather lay ill for two years, Yuan constantly matched his food intake to whatever his grandfather ate, never removing his hat and robes, attending him morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, when his grandfather lay ill for two years, Yuan continually adjusted what he ate according to his grandfather's appetite, never removing his hat and robes, attending him morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 及祖沒，號踴絕而後蘇。

translations.literal: When his grandfather died, he wailed and stamped in mourning until he lost consciousness, afterward reviving.
translations.idiomatic: When his grandfather died, he wailed and performed the mourning dance until he collapsed without breath, then revived.

sentences.zh: 隨其父，水漿不入口三日。

translations.literal: Following his father in mourning, he took neither water nor broth for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Following his father in mourning, he took neither water nor broth for three days.

sentences.zh: 鄉里咸歎異之。

translations.literal: Everyone in the neighborhood sighed in wonder at him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the neighborhood marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 縣博士楊軌等二百餘人上其狀，有詔表其門閭。

translations.literal: More than two hundred men including the county erudite Yang Gui submitted reports on his case; an imperial decree marked his gate and lane with honor.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred men, including the county erudite Yang Gui, submitted memorials on his case, and an imperial decree marked his gate and lane with honor.

sentences.zh: 王頒，字景彥，太原祁人也。

translations.literal: Wang Ban, courtesy name Jingyan, was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ban, courtesy name Jingyan, came from Qi in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父僧辯，《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: His father Sengbian has a biography in the Book of Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Sengbian has a biography in the Book of Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 頒少俶儻，有文武幹局。

translations.literal: Ban from youth was bold and free-spirited, with both literary and martial talent and enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Ban was bold and free-spirited, possessed of both literary and martial talent and enterprise.

sentences.zh: 僧辯平侯景，留頒荊州。

translations.literal: When Sengbian put down Hou Jing, he left Ban in Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengbian suppressed Hou Jing, he left Ban in Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 遇梁元帝為周師所陷，頒因入關。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang was captured by the Zhou army, Ban thereupon entered the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang fell to the Zhou army, Ban entered the Pass and came into Zhou territory.

sentences.zh: 聞其父為陳武帝所殺，號慟而絕，食頃乃蘇，哭不絕聲，毀瘠骨立。

translations.literal: When he heard his father had been killed by Emperor Wu of Chen, he wailed and collapsed unconscious; after the time it takes to eat a meal he revived, weeping without cease until he wasted away to skin and bones.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that his father had been killed by Emperor Wu of Chen, he wailed until he lost consciousness; after the time it takes to eat a meal he revived, and wept without ceasing until his grief wasted him to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 至服闋，常布衣蔬食，藉槁而臥。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he constantly wore plain clothes, ate vegetables, and slept on straw.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, he continued to wear plain clothes and eat simple vegetables, sleeping on a bed of straw.

sentences.zh: 周明帝嘉之，召授左侍上士。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Zhou commended him and summoned him to appoint him Left Attendant Senior Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Zhou was moved by his conduct and summoned him to appoint him Left Attendant Senior Officer.

sentences.zh: 累遷漢中太守，尋拜儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to governor of Hanzhong, and soon appointed Grand Master of Equal Rank with the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to governor of Hanzhong and was soon appointed to the rank of Grand Master of Equal Rank with the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，以平蠻功，加開府，封蛇丘縣公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui's Kaihuang era, for merit in suppressing the barbarians, he was granted the title of General Who Opens Offices and enfeoffed as Duke of Sheqiu County.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Sui Kaihuang era, for his merit in suppressing the barbarians, he was granted the title of General Who Opens Offices and enfeoffed as Duke of Sheqiu County.

sentences.zh: 獻取陳之策，上覽而異之，召見，言畢歔欷，上為之改容。

translations.literal: He submitted a plan for conquering Chen; the emperor read it with wonder, summoned him for an audience, and when he finished speaking sighed and wept; the emperor changed countenance on his account.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a plan for conquering Chen. The emperor read it with astonishment and summoned him for an audience; when Ban finished speaking the emperor sighed and wept, his expression completely changed.

sentences.zh: 及大舉伐陳，頒自請行。

translations.literal: When the great campaign to attack Chen was launched, Ban asked in person to take the field.
translations.idiomatic: When the great campaign against Chen was launched, Ban volunteered to go to the front.

sentences.zh: 率兵數百人，從韓擒虎先鋒夜濟，力戰被傷。

translations.literal: Leading several hundred soldiers, he followed General Han Qinhu's vanguard in a night crossing, fought fiercely, and was wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Leading several hundred men, he followed Han Qinhu's vanguard across the river by night, fought fiercely, and was wounded.

sentences.zh: 恐不堪復鬥，悲感嗚咽。

translations.literal: Fearing he could not fight again, he was moved to grief and sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he could not fight again, he was overcome with grief and sobbed.

sentences.zh: 夜中睡，夢有人授藥，比寤而瘡不痛。

translations.literal: As he slept at night, he dreamed someone gave him medicine; when he awoke his wounds did not hurt.
translations.idiomatic: As he slept at night he dreamed that someone gave him medicine; when he awoke his wounds no longer pained him.

sentences.zh: 時人以為孝感。

translations.literal: People at the time regarded it as filial piety moving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time regarded it as Heaven responding to filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 及陳滅，頒密召父在時士卒，得千餘人，對之涕泣。

translations.literal: When Chen was destroyed, Ban secretly summoned the troops who had served under his father, gathering more than a thousand; face to face with them he wept.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen was destroyed, Ban secretly summoned more than a thousand soldiers who had served under his father and wept before them.

sentences.zh: 其間壯士或問曰：「郎君仇恥已雪，而悲哀不止者，將不為霸先早死，不得手刃之邪？

translations.literal: Among them a brave man asked: "My lord, your vengeance and shame have been washed away; yet you cease not in sorrow—is it not because Baxian died too early for you to slay him with your own hand?
translations.idiomatic: Among them a warrior asked, "My lord, your vengeance has been achieved—why does your grief still not cease? Is it because Chen Baxian died too soon for you to kill him with your own hand?

sentences.zh: 請發其丘隴，鬥櫬焚骨，亦可申孝心矣。

translations.literal: Please let us open his mound, load his coffin into a cart, and burn his bones—you could thereby express your filial heart.
translations.idiomatic: Please let us open his tomb, load the coffin onto a cart, and burn his bones—that would at least give full expression to your filial heart.

sentences.zh: 」頒頓桑陳謝，額盡流血，答曰：「其為墳塋甚大，恐一宵發掘，不及其屍，更至明朝，事乃彰露。

translations.literal: Ban repeatedly bowed his head in apology until his brow bled streaming, and answered: "His tomb mound is very large; I fear that in one night's digging we would not reach the corpse; by morning the affair would be exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Ban bowed his head repeatedly in apology until blood streamed from his brow and answered, "His tomb mound is very large. I fear that opening it in a single night would not let us reach the corpse, and by the next morning the affair would be exposed.

sentences.zh: 」諸人請具鍬鍤。

translations.literal: The men asked to prepare shovels and mattocks.
translations.idiomatic: The men offered to bring spades and mattocks.

sentences.zh: 於是夜發其陵，剖棺，見陳武帝須皆不落，其本皆出自骨中。

translations.literal: Thereupon that night they opened his tomb and opened the coffin; they saw that Emperor Wu of Chen's whiskers had not fallen—each one grew from the bone itself.
translations.idiomatic: That night they opened the tomb and broke into the coffin. Chen Wudi's whiskers had not fallen out at all; each one still grew from the bone itself.

sentences.zh: 頒遂焚骨取灰，投水飲之。

translations.literal: Ban then burned the bones, took the ashes, mixed them with water, and drank them.
translations.idiomatic: Ban then burned the bones, mixed the ashes with water, and drank the mixture.

sentences.zh: 既而自縛歸罪。

translations.literal: Then he bound himself and surrendered to accept punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He then bound his own hands and surrendered to face punishment.

sentences.zh: 晉王表其狀。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin memorialized the court about his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin memorialized the court about what he had done.

sentences.zh: 文帝曰：「朕以義平陳。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said: "I conquered Chen in the name of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said, "I conquered Chen in the name of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 王頒所為，亦孝義之道，何忍罪之？

translations.literal: What Wang Ban has done is also the Way of filial piety and righteousness—how could I bear to punish him?
translations.idiomatic: What Wang Ban has done is likewise the Way of filial piety and righteousness. How could I bear to punish him?

sentences.zh: 」舍而不問。

translations.literal: He pardoned him without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned him without further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 有司錄其戰功，將加柱國，賜物五千段。

translations.literal: The responsible officials recorded his battle merit, intending to promote him to pillar of state and bestow five thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials recorded his battle merit and proposed promoting him to Pillar of State and bestowing five thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 頒固辭曰：「臣緣國威靈，得雪怨恥，本心徇私，非是為國。

translations.literal: Ban firmly declined and said: "I, by the state's august power, was able to wash away hatred and shame; my heart's motive was private feeling, not service to the state.
