translations.idiomatic: Ban firmly refused, saying, "Through the state's august power I was able to wash away my hatred and shame. My motive was private feeling, not service to the state.

sentences.zh: 所加官賞，終不敢當。

translations.literal: The rank and reward offered—I dare not accept them in the end.
translations.idiomatic: The rank and rewards offered, I dare not accept.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted his wish.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor acquiesced.

sentences.zh: 拜代州刺史，甚有惠政。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of Dai Province and governed with great benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Dai Province and governed with considerable benevolence.

sentences.zh: 卒于齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He died while serving as governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 弟頍，字景文。

translations.literal: His younger brother Hui, courtesy name Jingwen.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wang Hui, courtesy name Jingwen.

sentences.zh: 年數歲而江陵亡，同諸兄入關。

translations.literal: When he was only a few years old, Jiangling fell; together with his elder brothers he entered the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When he was still very young Jiangling fell, and he entered the Pass together with his elder brothers.

sentences.zh: 少好遊俠，年二十，尚不知書，為其兄顒所責怒。

translations.literal: In youth he loved wandering and knight-errantry; at twenty he still did not know books, and was scolded and rebuked by his elder brother Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was fond of wandering and knight-errantry. At twenty he still could not read and was fiercely scolded by his elder brother Yong.

sentences.zh: 於是感激，始讀《孝經》、《論語》，晝夜不倦，遂讀《左傳》、《禮》、《易》、《詩》、《書》，乃歎曰：「書無不可讀者。

translations.literal: Thereupon stirred to his senses, he began reading the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, day and night without weariness; he went on to read the Zuo Commentary, the Book of Rites, the Book of Changes, the Book of Poetry, and the Book of Documents, and sighed: "There is nothing in books that cannot be read.
translations.idiomatic: Stirred to his senses by this, he began reading the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, studying day and night without fatigue, then read the Zuo Commentary, the Book of Rites, the Book of Changes, the Book of Poetry, and the Book of Documents, and sighed, "There is nothing in books that cannot be read.

sentences.zh: 」勤學累載，遂遍通《五經》，究其旨趣，大為儒者所稱。

translations.literal: After diligent study over many years, he thoroughly mastered the Five Classics, plumbed their meaning and import, and was greatly praised by Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: After many years of diligent study he mastered all five classics, penetrated their meaning, and was greatly praised by Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 解綴文，善談話。

translations.literal: He could compose linked prose and was skilled in conversation.
translations.idiomatic: He could compose linked prose and was skilled in conversation.

sentences.zh: 年三十，周武帝引為露門學士，每有議決，多頍所為。

translations.literal: At thirty, Emperor Wu of Zhou summoned him as a scholar of the Lumen Gate; whenever there were deliberations and decisions, it was mostly Hui who made them.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty, Emperor Wu of Zhou took him as a scholar of the Lumen Gate; whenever important decisions were made, it was most often Hui who made them.

sentences.zh: 性識甄明，精力不倦，好讀諸子，遍記異書，以博物稱。

translations.literal: By nature he had keen discernment and tireless energy; he loved reading the various masters and memorized unusual books, and was known for broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: He had keen discernment and tireless energy, loved reading the various masters and unusual books, and was known for his encyclopedic learning.

sentences.zh: 又曉兵法，益有從橫之志，每歎不逢時，常以將相自許。

translations.literal: He also understood military strategy and grew ever more ambitious in alliance and stratagem; he often lamented that the times did not meet him, and frequently looked on himself as destined for general or minister.
translations.idiomatic: He also understood military strategy and grew ever more ambitious for the arts of alliance and stratagem; he often lamented that the times did not favor him and frequently regarded himself as destined for general or minister.

sentences.zh: 開皇五年，授著作佐郎，尋令于國子講授。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaihuang, he was appointed Assistant Director of the Bureau of Authorship, and soon afterward was ordered to lecture at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaihuang he was appointed Assistant Director of the Bureau of Authorship and was soon ordered to lecture at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 會帝親臨釋奠。

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor came in person for the sacrifice to Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the emperor came in person to the Confucian sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒元善講《孝經》，頍與相論難，詞義鋒起，善往往見屈。

translations.literal: The Academic Director Yuan Shan lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety; Hui debated with him, their words and arguments sharp as blades, and Shan was often put to rout.
translations.idiomatic: The Academic Director Yuan Shan lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety; Hui debated with him in sharp argument, and Shan was often defeated.

sentences.zh: 帝大奇之，超授國子博士。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly amazed and promoted him in exceptional fashion to Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly astonished and exceptionally promoted him to Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 後坐事解職，配防嶺南。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed from office for an offense and was sentenced to guard duty in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was dismissed from office for an offense and was sentenced to guard duty in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 數載，授漢王諒府諮議參軍，王甚禮之。

translations.literal: Several years later, he was appointed Consulting Adjutant on the staff of Prince Liang of Han; the prince treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was appointed Consulting Adjutant on the staff of Prince Liang of Han, who treated him with great courtesy.

sentences.zh: 時諒見房陵及秦、蜀二王相次廢黜，潛有異志。

translations.literal: At that time the prince saw that Prince of Fangling and the Princes of Qin and Shu had been deposed one after another, and secretly harbored rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Liang saw that the Prince of Fangling and the Princes of Qin and Shu had been deposed one after another, and secretly harbored rebellious intent.

sentences.zh: 頍陰勸諒繕甲兵。

translations.literal: Hui secretly urged the prince to repair weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Hui secretly urged the prince to gather weapons and armor.

sentences.zh: 及文帝崩，諒遂舉兵反，多頍之計也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen died, the prince thereupon raised troops in rebellion; much of the plan came from Hui.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen died, the prince raised troops in rebellion; much of the plan came from Hui.

sentences.zh: 頍後數進奇策，諒不能用。

translations.literal: Hui later submitted several clever stratagems, but the prince would not employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Hui later submitted several clever stratagems, but the prince would not adopt them.

sentences.zh: 楊素至蒿澤，將戰。

translations.literal: Yang Su reached Haozhe and was about to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su reached Haozhe and was about to give battle.

sentences.zh: 頍謂其子曰：「氣候殊不佳，兵必敗。

translations.literal: Hui said to his son: "The omens are very unfavorable; the army is sure to be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Hui said to his son, "The omens are very unfavorable; the army is sure to be defeated.

sentences.zh: 汝可隨從我。

translations.literal: You may follow along with me.
translations.idiomatic: You may come with me.

sentences.zh: 」既而兵敗，頍將歸突厥。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the army was defeated; Hui intended to flee to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the army was defeated and Hui intended to flee to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 至山中，徑路斷絕，知必不免。

translations.literal: Reaching the mountains, the paths were cut off; he knew he could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the mountains, the paths were cut off and he knew he could not escape.

sentences.zh: 謂其子曰：「吾之計謀，不減楊素，但為言不見從，遂至於此。

translations.literal: He said to his son: "My stratagems are no less than Yang Su's, but because my words were not heeded, it has come to this.
translations.idiomatic: He said to his son, "My stratagems are no less than Yang Su's, but because my advice was not heeded, it has come to this.

sentences.zh: 不能坐受禽執，以成豎子之名也。

translations.literal: I cannot sit and allow myself to be captured and become a byword for some stripling.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot sit and allow myself to be captured and become a laughingstock for some stripling.

sentences.zh: 吾死後，汝慎勿過親故！

translations.literal: After I am dead, you must be careful not to visit kinsmen and old friends!
translations.idiomatic: After I am dead, you must be careful not to visit kinsmen and old friends!

sentences.zh: 」於是自殺，瘞之石窟中。

translations.literal: Thereupon he killed himself and was buried in a stone cave.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he killed himself and was buried in a stone cave.

sentences.zh: 其子數日不得食，遂過其故人，竟為所禽。

translations.literal: His son went several days without food; he then visited an old friend and was ultimately captured.
translations.idiomatic: His son went several days without food, then visited an old friend and was ultimately captured.

sentences.zh: 楊素求頍屍得之，斬首，梟於太原。

translations.literal: Yang Su sought out Hui's corpse, obtained it, cut off the head, and displayed it at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su sought out Hui's corpse, obtained it, cut off the head, and displayed it at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 所撰《五經大義》三十卷，有集二十卷，並因兵亂，無復存焉。

translations.literal: The thirty juan of his Five Classics with Commentary that he composed, and the twenty juan of his collected writings, were all lost in the turmoil of war and no longer survive.
translations.idiomatic: The thirty juan of his Five Classics with Commentary and the twenty juan of his collected writings were all lost in the turmoil of war and no longer survive.

sentences.zh: 楊慶，字伯悅，河間人也。

translations.literal: Yang Qing, courtesy name Boyue, was a native of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qing, courtesy name Boyue, came from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 祖玄、父剛，並以至孝知名。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xuan and his father Gang were both well known for supreme filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xuan and his father Gang were both well known for supreme filial piety.

sentences.zh: 慶美容止，性辯慧。

translations.literal: Qing had a handsome appearance and was by nature eloquent and intelligent.
translations.idiomatic: Qing had a handsome appearance and was by nature eloquent and intelligent.

sentences.zh: 年十六，齊國子博士徐遵明見而異之。

translations.literal: At sixteen, Xu Zunming, Erudite of the Qi Imperial Academy, saw him and marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen, Xu Zunming, Erudite of the Qi Imperial Academy, saw him and was struck by his talent.

sentences.zh: 及長，頗涉書記。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he gained considerable knowledge of writing and records.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he gained considerable knowledge of writing and recordkeeping.

sentences.zh: 年二十五，郡察孝廉，以侍養不赴。

translations.literal: At twenty-five the commandery nominated him as Filial and Incorrupt; because he was serving and supporting his parents he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-five the commandery nominated him as Filial and Incorrupt, but because he was serving and supporting his parents he did not respond to the summons.

sentences.zh: 母有疾，不解襟帶者七旬。

translations.literal: When his mother was ill, he did not undo his sash and belt for seventy days.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother was ill, he did not undo his sash and belt for seventy days.

sentences.zh: 及居母憂，哀毀骨立，負土成墳。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning for his mother, his grief wasted him to skin and bones, and he carried earth to build the grave mound.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered mourning for his mother, his grief wasted him to skin and bone, and he carried earth to build the grave mound.

sentences.zh: 齊文宣表其門閭，賜帛及綿粟各有差。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan of Qi marked his gate and lane with honor and bestowed silk and cotton grain, each in fixed measure.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan of Qi marked his gate and lane with honor and bestowed silk and cotton grain, each in fixed measure.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，屢加褒賞，擢授儀同三司，板平陽太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he repeatedly added praise and rewards, promoted him to Grand Master of Equal Rank with the Three Dukes, and appointed him in provisional office as governor of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he repeatedly added praise and rewards, promoted Qing to Grand Master of Equal Rank with the Three Ducal Ministers, and provisionally appointed him governor of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 田翼，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Tian Yi—his place of origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yi—his place of origin is unknown.

sentences.zh: 養母以孝聞。

translations.literal: He supported his mother and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He supported his mother and was renowned for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 其後母臥疾歲餘，翼親易燥濕，母食則食，母不食則不食。

translations.literal: When his stepmother was bedridden with illness for more than a year, Yi personally changed her bedding when wet or dry; when she ate, he ate; when she did not eat, he did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: When his stepmother lay ill in bed for more than a year, Yi personally changed her bedding whenever it grew damp or dry. When she ate, he ate; when she refused food, he refused food as well.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，母患暴痢。

translations.literal: During the Kaihuang era of Sui, his mother suffered from acute dysentery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang reign of Sui, his mother was stricken with violent dysentery.

sentences.zh: 翼謂中毒藥，遂親嘗穢惡。

translations.literal: Yi thought it was poisoned medicine and so personally tasted the foul discharge.
translations.idiomatic: Yi suspected poisoned medicine and personally tasted her foul discharge to test it.

sentences.zh: 母終，翼一慟而絕。

translations.literal: When his mother died, Yi died in a single burst of grief.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, Yi gave one great cry of grief and expired.

sentences.zh: 妻亦不勝哀而死。

translations.literal: His wife also could not bear the grief and died.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, too, could not endure the grief and died.

sentences.zh: 鄉人厚共葬之。

translations.literal: The villagers generously joined together to bury them.
translations.idiomatic: The villagers generously pooled their resources and buried them together.

sentences.zh: 紐因，字孝政，河東安邑人也。

translations.literal: Niu Yin, courtesy name Xiaozheng, was a native of Anyi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Yin, courtesy name Xiaozheng, came from Anyi in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 性至孝。

translations.literal: By nature he was extremely filial.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was profoundly filial.

sentences.zh: 周武成中，父母喪，廬於墓側，負土成墳。

translations.literal: During the Wucheng era of Northern Zhou, when his parents died, he built a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to form the grave mound.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wucheng reign of Northern Zhou, when his parents died, he built a mourning hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build up the grave mound.

sentences.zh: 廬前生麻一株，高丈許，圍之合拱，枝葉鬱茂，冬夏恆青。

translations.literal: Before his hut a hemp plant grew, about a zhang tall, its girth spanning two arm-lengths, its branches and leaves lush; winter and summer it stayed green.
translations.idiomatic: Before his hut a hemp plant sprang up, nearly a zhang in height, its trunk thick enough to span with both arms, its branches and leaves luxuriant and green through winter and summer alike.

sentences.zh: 有鳥棲上，因舉聲哭，鳥即悲鳴。

translations.literal: A bird roosted upon it; when Yin raised his voice in weeping, the bird at once wailed mournfully.
translations.idiomatic: A bird nested in it; whenever Yin lifted his voice in weeping, the bird at once answered with mournful cries.

sentences.zh: 時人異之。

translations.literal: People of the time marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time regarded this as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 周武帝表其閭，擢授甘棠令。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou honored his lane with a memorial and promoted him to Magistrate of Gantang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou marked his lane with honor and appointed him magistrate of Gantang.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of the Kaihuang era of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Kaihuang reign of Sui.

sentences.zh: 子士雄，少質直孝友。

translations.literal: His son Shixiong was from youth straightforward, filial, and fraternal.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shixiong was from youth honest, filial, and devoted to his brothers.

sentences.zh: 喪父，復廬於墓側，負土成墳。

translations.literal: When his father died, he again built a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to form the grave mound.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he again built a mourning hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build up the grave mound.

sentences.zh: 其庭前有一槐樹，先甚鬱茂，及士雄居喪，樹遂枯死。

translations.literal: In the courtyard before his house stood a pagoda tree, formerly very lush; when Shixiong entered mourning, the tree withered and died.
translations.idiomatic: A pagoda tree stood in the courtyard before his house, once flourishing and dense; when Shixiong entered mourning, the tree withered and died.

sentences.zh: 服闋還宅，死槐復榮。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended and he returned home, the dead pagoda tree revived and flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended and he returned home, the dead pagoda tree put forth leaves and flourished once more.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝聞之，歎其父子至孝，下詔褒揚，號其居為累德里。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui heard of this, he sighed at the father and son's supreme filial piety, issued an edict praising them, and named their residence Leide Lane.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui heard of this, he sighed at the supreme filial piety of father and son, issued an edict praising them, and named their dwelling Accumulated Virtue Lane.

sentences.zh: 劉仕俊，彭城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Shijun was a native of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shijun came from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 性至孝。

translations.literal: By nature he was extremely filial.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was profoundly filial.

sentences.zh: 丁母喪，絕而復蘇者數矣，勺飲不入口者七日。

translations.literal: During mourning for his mother, he repeatedly stopped breathing and revived; for seven days he took not a spoonful of drink into his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his mother, he repeatedly stopped breathing and came back to life; for seven days he would not take even a spoonful of water.

sentences.zh: 廬於墓側，負土成墳，列植松柏，虎狼馴擾，為之取食。

translations.literal: He built a hut beside the tomb, carried earth to form the grave mound, and planted pine and cypress in rows; tigers and wolves were tame in his presence and brought him food.
translations.idiomatic: He built a mourning hut beside the tomb, carried earth to build up the grave mound, and planted rows of pine and cypress. Tigers and wolves grew tame around him and even brought him food.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，表其門閭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he honored Shijun's gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he marked Shijun's gate and lane with honor.

sentences.zh: 翟普林，楚丘人也。

translations.literal: Zhai Pulü was a native of Chuqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Pulü came from Chuqiu.

sentences.zh: 事親以孝聞。

translations.literal: He served his parents and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He served his parents and was renowned for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 州郡辟皆不就，躬耕色養。

translations.literal: Invitations from prefectures and commanderies he all declined; he personally tilled the fields and supported his parents with cheerful devotion.
translations.idiomatic: He declined every invitation from prefectural and commandery offices, tilled the fields himself, and supported his parents with cheerful, attentive care.

sentences.zh: 鄉閭謂為楚丘先生。

translations.literal: The townsfolk called him the Master of Chuqiu.
translations.idiomatic: People in the village called him the Master of Chuqiu.

sentences.zh: 後父母疾，親易澡濕，不解衣者七旬。

translations.literal: Later, when his parents fell ill, he personally changed their bedding when wet; he did not undress for seventy days.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his parents fell ill, he personally changed their bedding whenever it grew damp and did not undress for seventy days.

sentences.zh: 大業初，父母俱終，哀毀殆將滅性。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daye era, both parents died; his grief and self-wasting nearly destroyed his life.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daye reign, both parents died; his grief wasted him nearly to death.

sentences.zh: 廬於墓側，負土成墳。

translations.literal: He built a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to form the grave mound.
translations.idiomatic: He built a mourning hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build up the grave mound.

sentences.zh: 盛冬不衣繒絮，唯著單縗而已。

translations.literal: In deep winter he wore no silk or cotton padding, only a single garment of hemp mourning cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Even in the depths of winter he wore no silk or cotton padding, only a single hemp mourning garment.

sentences.zh: 家有鳥犬，隨其在墓，若普林哀臨，犬亦悲號，見者嗟異。

translations.literal: The birds and dogs in his household followed him to the tomb; whenever Pulü wept in grief, the dogs also wailed mournfully; those who saw this sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: The birds and dogs of his household followed him to the tomb. Whenever Pulü wept in grief, the dogs wailed as well; all who saw it sighed in wonder.

sentences.zh: 有二鵲巢其廬前柏樹，入廬馴狎，無所驚懼。

translations.literal: Two magpies nested in the cypress before his hut; entering the hut they were tame and familiar, showing no fear.
translations.idiomatic: Two magpies nested in the cypress before his hut; they entered the hut freely, tame and unafraid.

sentences.zh: 司隸巡察，奏其孝感，擢授孝陽令。

translations.literal: The Regional Inspector on tour reported his filial responsiveness, and he was promoted to Magistrate of Xiaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Regional Inspector, on his inspection tour, reported Pulü's filial responsiveness to the throne, and he was appointed magistrate of Xiaoyang.

sentences.zh: 華秋，汲郡臨河人也。

translations.literal: Hua Qiu was a native of Linhe in Jijun.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Qiu came from Linhe in Jijun commandery.

sentences.zh: 幼喪父，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: He lost his father in youth and served his mother, becoming known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father in youth and served his mother with such devotion that he became known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 家貧，傭賃為養。

translations.literal: The family was poor; he hired himself out for wages to support them.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor, so he hired himself out for wages to support them.

sentences.zh: 其母患疾，秋容貌毀悴，鬢須盡改。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, Qiu's appearance was wasted and haggard; his temples and beard were wholly altered.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, Qiu's face grew haggard and wasted; even his temples and beard turned gray.

sentences.zh: 母終，遂絕櫛沐，發盡禿落。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he ceased combing and bathing; his hair fell out entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he stopped combing and bathing, and his hair fell out completely.

sentences.zh: 廬於墓側，負土成墳。

translations.literal: He built a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to form the grave mound.
translations.idiomatic: He built a mourning hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build up the grave mound.

sentences.zh: 有人欲助之者，秋輒拜而止之。

translations.literal: When anyone wished to help him, Qiu would bow and stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever anyone offered to help, Qiu would bow and refuse.

sentences.zh: 隋大業初，調狐皮，郡縣大獵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye in Sui, fox pelts were levied as tribute; the commandery and counties mounted a great hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daye reign of Sui, fox pelts were levied as tribute, and the commandery and counties organized a great hunt.

sentences.zh: 有一兔，逐之，奔入秋廬中，匿秋膝下。

translations.literal: A rabbit was pursued; fleeing, it ran into Qiu's mourning hut and hid beneath his knees.
translations.idiomatic: One rabbit, pursued by hunters, fled into Qiu's mourning hut and hid beneath his knees.

sentences.zh: 獵人至廬所，異而免之。

translations.literal: When the hunters came to the hut, they marveled and spared it.
translations.idiomatic: When the hunters reached the hut, they marveled at the sight and spared the rabbit.

sentences.zh: 自爾，此兔常宿廬中，馴其左右。

translations.literal: From then on this rabbit often lodged in the hut and was tame at his side.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the rabbit often slept in the hut and grew tame at his side.

sentences.zh: 郡縣嘉其孝感，具以狀聞。

translations.literal: The commandery and county praised his filial responsiveness and reported the full particulars to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery and county praised his filial responsiveness and submitted a full report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 降使勞問，而表其門閭。

translations.literal: Emissaries were sent down to console him, and his gate and lane were honored.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent emissaries to console him and marked his gate and lane with honor.

sentences.zh: 後群盜起，常往來廬之左右，咸相誡曰：「勿犯孝子鄉。

translations.literal: Later, when bandits rose in numbers, they often passed near his hut; all warned one another, saying, "Do not violate the Village of the Filial Son."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when bandits rose in numbers, they often passed near his hut, and all warned one another: "Do not violate the Village of the Filial Son."

sentences.zh: 」賴秋全者甚眾。

translations.literal: Thanks to Qiu, very many were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Very many people were spared, thanks to Qiu.

sentences.zh: 徐孝肅，汲郡人也。

translations.literal: Xu Xiaosu was a native of Jijun.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiaosu came from Jijun commandery.

sentences.zh: 宗族數十家，多以豪侈相尚，唯孝肅儉約。

translations.literal: Among dozens of clansmen, most competed in extravagance; only Xiaosu was frugal.
translations.idiomatic: Among dozens of clans in his lineage, most vied in luxury and display; only Xiaosu lived frugally.

sentences.zh: 事親以孝聞。

translations.literal: He served his parents and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He served his parents and was renowned for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 雖在幼小，宗黨間每有爭訟，皆至孝肅所平論，短者無不引咎而退。

translations.literal: Even while still young, whenever clansmen had disputes, all came to Xiaosu for judgment; the one at fault always acknowledged guilt and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Even while still young, whenever clansmen quarreled, all brought their disputes to Xiaosu for judgment; the one in the wrong always accepted blame and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 孝肅早孤，不識父。

translations.literal: Xiaosu was orphaned early and never knew his father.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosu was orphaned early and never knew his father.

sentences.zh: 及長，問其母父狀，因畫工圖其形，構廟置之而定省焉，朔望享祭。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he asked his mother about his father's appearance; he then had an artist paint his likeness, built a shrine and placed the portrait there, attending morning and evening; on the first and fifteenth of each month he offered sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he asked his mother what his father had looked like, then had a painter render his likeness, built a shrine, and placed the portrait there for daily morning and evening attendance and sacrifice on the first and fifteenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 養母至孝，數十年家人未見其忿恚色。

translations.literal: He supported his mother with utmost filial piety; for decades his household never saw him show anger.
translations.idiomatic: He supported his mother with the utmost filial devotion; for decades his household never once saw him show anger.

sentences.zh: 母老疾，孝肅視易燥濕，憂悴數年，見者莫不悲悼。

translations.literal: When his mother grew old and ill, Xiaosu watched and changed her bedding when wet or dry; for years he was wan with worry; all who saw him were filled with sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother grew old and ill, Xiaosu tended her day and night, changing her bedding whenever it grew damp or dry. For years he wasted away with worry, and all who saw him were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 母終，孝肅茹蔬飲水，盛冬單縗，毀瘠骨立。

translations.literal: When his mother died, Xiaosu ate vegetables and drank water, wore only a single hemp mourning garment in deep winter, and was wasted to skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, Xiaosu ate only vegetables and drank water, wore nothing but a single hemp mourning garment even in deep winter, and was wasted to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 祖父母、父母墓，皆負土成墳。

translations.literal: At the graves of his grandparents and parents, he all carried earth to form the mounds.
translations.idiomatic: At the graves of his grandparents and parents alike, he carried earth to build up the mounds.

sentences.zh: 廬于墓所四十餘載，被髮徒跣，遂以終身。

translations.literal: He dwelt at the graveside for more than forty years, hair disheveled and barefoot, and so remained to the end of his life.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at the graveside for more than forty years, hair unbound and barefoot, and so remained for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 其弟德備終，子處默，又廬於墓側。

translations.literal: When his younger brother Debei died, his son Chumo again built a hut beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When his younger brother Debei died, Debei's son Chumo again built a mourning hut beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 弈世稱孝焉。

translations.literal: For generations they were called filial.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family was celebrated for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 論曰：塞天地而橫四海者，唯孝而已矣。

translations.literal: Commentary: That which fills Heaven and Earth and spans the four seas is filial piety alone.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Only filial piety fills Heaven and Earth and extends across the four seas.

sentences.zh: 然則孝始愛敬之方，終極哀思之道，厥亦多緒，其心一焉。

translations.literal: Filial piety begins with loving reverence and reaches the utmost in paths of mourning grief; its manifestations are many, yet the heart is one.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety begins in love and reverence and finds its fullest expression in the depths of mourning grief. Its outward forms are many, but the heart behind them is one.

sentences.zh: 若上智稟自然之質，中庸有企及之義，及其成名，其美一也。

translations.literal: The highest wisdom receives heaven-endowed nature; the middle way holds meaning one may strive toward; when they achieve renown, their excellence is one.
translations.idiomatic: The highest wisdom is endowed with nature itself; the middling person can still aspire to its meaning. Yet when they achieve renown, the beauty of their achievement is the same.

sentences.zh: 長孫慮等或出公卿之緒，藉禮教之資；

translations.literal: Zhangsun Lü and the others were perhaps of ministerial and noble lineage, drawing on ritual and instruction;
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Lü and the others came from ministerial and noble families and drew on the resources of ritual teaching;

sentences.zh: 或出茆笪之下，非獎勸所得。

translations.literal: or sprang from thatched hovels, not obtained through reward and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: others rose from grass-thatched hovels, with no reward or encouragement to account for their virtue.

sentences.zh: 並因心乘理，不逾禮教，感通所致，貫之神明。

translations.literal: All followed the heart and took hold of principle, not transgressing ritual teaching; what they attained through responsive communion penetrates to the spirits and the divine.
translations.idiomatic: All acted from the heart and in accord with principle, never overstepping ritual teaching. What they achieved through responsive communion with Heaven reached even the spirits and the divine.

sentences.zh: 乃有負土成墳，致毀滅性，雖乖先王之典制，亦觀過而知仁矣。

translations.literal: Some carried earth to form grave mounds and brought themselves to the brink of self-destruction; though this diverges from the ancient kings' institutions, one may yet observe the fault and perceive their humaneness.
translations.idiomatic: Some carried earth to build grave mounds and brought themselves near to self-destruction. Though this departs from the institutions of the ancient kings, one may still observe the excess and recognize the humaneness within it.
